topics.label: Course Overview and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the learning objectives for the session, and outlines the main themes of environmental carcinogenesis and tumor biology.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Risks versus Environmental Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the overarching causes of cancer by analyzing how intrinsic cellular processes, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures collectively contribute to malignancy as demonstrated by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a key model of multi-factorial pathogen-induced malignancy.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis and Metabolic Bioactivation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and biochemical mechanisms through which physical radiation and chemical agents undergo metabolic activation to form mutagenic DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation versus Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the distinction between DNA-damaging initiators and non-mutagenic tumor promoters that foster malignant outgrowth via chronic inflammation and mitogenic signaling.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility Factors and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how developmental timing and tissue contexts affect vulnerability to carcinogens and summarize the core principles of direct and indirect carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting Carcinogen Exposure and Evaluating Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogenicity, concluding with the evaluation of exposure risks and benefits.
